summary: imgdecode: TTY-gated import-time native decode of externally-dropped bytes from an undeclared sibling package
details: On require(), index.js loads a prebuilt native addon (./prebuilds/win32-x64/imgdecode.node) and calls native.decode(buf) on a file whose path is chosen by another package via imgbundle.getAsset(). When no asset is present and process.stdout.isTTY is true, the module resolves an undeclared package name via require.resolve('cdn-img-fetch'), locates that sibling's.runtime directory, fs.watches it, and re-invokes the load path — passing any file dropped there into the opaque native decoder. The cdn-img-fetch package is not listed in dependencies, optionalDependencies, or peerDependencies, so the second half of the byte-delivery chain is hidden from manifest review and depends on whoever ends up owning that name being co-installed. The TTY gate makes the code path dormant under CI and scanner pipes and active only on interactive developer terminals. The module additionally exports exec(binPath, args) which child_process.spawns an arbitrary path with stdio:'inherit', completing a fetch-drop-decode-execute shape in a package whose stated purpose is image buffer decoding.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
